en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to METICULOUS.
en.e: A meticulous worker pays close attention to every detail.

en.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to BENEVOLENT.
en.e: Benevolent means well-meaning and kind; malevolent means wishing harm.

en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to UBIQUITOUS.
en.e: Smartphones have become ubiquitous.

en.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to FRUGAL.
en.e: Frugal means careful with money; extravagant means spending too much.

en.q: Neither the manager nor the employees ___ present at the meeting.
en.e: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("employees").

en.q: Each of the applicants ___ required to submit a valid ID.
en.e: "Each" is singular, so it takes a singular verb.

en.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Between you and I, the report is late.
Between you and me, the report is late.
Between yourself and I, the report is late.
Between me and I, the report is late.
en.e: "Between" is a preposition, so it takes the object pronoun "me."

en.q: DOCTOR is to HOSPITAL as TEACHER is to:
en.e: A doctor works in a hospital; a teacher works in a school.

en.q: PEN is to WRITE as KNIFE is to:
en.e: The relationship is tool to function.

en.q: BIRD is to FLOCK as FISH is to:
en.e: A group of fish is a school.

en.q: What does the idiom "burn the midnight oil" mean?
o: Work or study late into the night
en.e: Example: She burned the midnight oil to review for the exam.

en.q: What does "break the ice" mean?
o: Ease tension and start a conversation
en.e: A joke can help break the ice in a meeting.

en.q: Which word is spelled correctly?
en.e: Accommodate has a double "c" and a double "m."

en.q: Which word is spelled correctly?
en.e: Occurrence: double "c," double "r," and "-ence."

en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to CANDID.
en.e: A candid answer is honest and direct.

en.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to OBSOLETE.
en.e: Obsolete means no longer in use.

en.q: He is very good ___ mathematics.
en.e: We say "good at" a subject or skill.

en.q: By next year, she ___ in the agency for ten years.
en.e: The future perfect describes an action completed by a future time.

en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to ABROGATE.
en.e: To abrogate a law is to repeal or abolish it.

en.q: Which sentence uses the correct word?
o: The new policy will effect all employees.
The new policy will affect all employees.
The new policy will affects all employees.
The new policy will effecting all employees.
en.e: "Affect" is usually the verb; "effect" is usually the noun (the result).

en.q: "Public servants must perform their duties with integrity. Integrity means being honest and consistent even when no one is watching." According to the passage, integrity means:
o: Being honest and consistent even without supervision
en.e: The second sentence defines integrity directly.

en.q: "Mangroves protect coastal communities by reducing the force of waves during storms. They also serve as breeding grounds for fish." What is the main idea?
o: Mangroves benefit coastal communities in several ways.
en.e: The passage gives two benefits of mangroves.

en.q: "The office will shift to online appointments next month. Walk-in clients will still be served, but those with appointments will be prioritized." What can be inferred?
o: Walk-in clients will no longer be served.
Clients with online appointments will be served first.
The office will close next month.
en.e: The passage says appointment holders will be prioritized.

en.q: "Although the project was delayed by heavy rains, the bridge was completed within the approved budget." Which statement is true according to the sentence?
o: The project finished within budget despite the delay.
The rains did not affect the project.
en.e: "Although" introduces the delay; the main clause says it stayed within budget.

en.q: "Volunteerism strengthens communities. When citizens give their time, they build trust and solve local problems together." The word "strengthens" most nearly means:
en.e: Volunteerism makes communities stronger.

en.q: "Reading every day improves vocabulary. Students who read for 20 minutes daily encounter thousands of new words each year." What is the author's purpose?
en.e: The passage presents a benefit of reading every day.

en.q: "The memo instructs all personnel to submit their leave applications at least five working days before the intended leave." When should leave applications be submitted?
o: On the day of the leave
At least five working days before the leave
en.e: The memo states the five-working-day rule.

en.q: "Plastic waste clogs drainage systems, which can worsen flooding during heavy rain." What is the cause-and-effect relationship?
o: Plastic waste blocks drains, making flooding worse.
en.e: The cause is plastic waste; the effect is worse flooding.

en.q: "Maria was the first to arrive and the last to leave. She checked every document twice before signing." Which word best describes Maria?
en.e: Her actions show hard work and care.

en.q: Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph: (1) Finally, submit the form at window 3. (2) First, get a queue number. (3) Next, fill out the application form.
en.e: The transition words "First," "Next" and "Finally" show the order.

en.q: "Not all criticism is negative. Constructive criticism helps people improve their work." What does the passage suggest?
en.e: "Not all criticism is negative" introduces helpful criticism.

en.q: "The town's population doubled in ten years, but the number of public schools stayed the same." What problem is most likely implied?
en.e: More people with the same number of schools suggests overcrowding.

en.q: "Tourism brings income to the province; however, it can also damage fragile natural sites if not managed well." The word "however" signals:
en.e: "However" introduces an opposing idea.

en.q: "Early detection of diseases through regular check-ups can save lives and reduce medical costs." Which is the best title?
en.e: The sentence focuses on the benefits of regular check-ups.

en.q: "The applicant's explanation was plausible, so the panel accepted it." "Plausible" most nearly means:
en.e: The panel accepted it because it seemed believable.

en.q: "Only employees who have completed the training may operate the new system." Ana has not completed the training. What follows?
o: Ana may not operate the system yet.
en.e: Completing the training is a requirement.

en.q: "Rice prices rose sharply after typhoons damaged farms in several provinces." Why did rice prices rise?
o: Typhoons damaged farms and reduced supply.
en.e: Damaged farms reduced the supply of rice.

en.q: "Respect for others, punctuality and accountability are expected of every government employee." Which is NOT mentioned as expected behavior?
en.e: Seniority is not listed in the sentence.

en.q: "Water is essential to life. Yet millions of people still lack access to safe drinking water." The tone of the passage is mainly:
en.e: The contrast highlights a serious problem.

en.q: "The committee postponed the hearing indefinitely." "Indefinitely" means:
en.e: An indefinite postponement has no set new date.

en.q: What is 25% of 480?
An item costs ₱1,200. After a 15% discount, what is the price?
What is the average of 85, 90, 78 and 87?
What comes next in the series 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___?
en.e: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12.

en.q: What comes next in the series 3, 9, 27, 81, ___?
en.e: Each term is multiplied by 3.

en.q: ₱64 is divided between two people in the ratio 3:5. How much is the larger share?
What is the simple interest on ₱10,000 at 5% per year for 3 years?
A can finish a job in 6 days and B in 3 days. How long will they take working together?
en.e: Rates: 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 job per day, so 2 days.

en.q: A bus travels 240 km in 4 hours. What is its average speed?
What is 3/4 + 2/3?
Express 0.375 as a fraction in lowest terms.
A father is three times as old as his son. The sum of their ages is 48. How old is the son?
A salary increased from ₱20,000 to ₱25,000. What is the percentage increase?
What is the area of a rectangle 12 m long and 8 m wide?
en.e: Area = length × width = 12 × 8 = 96.

en.q: If 5 pencils cost ₱60, how much do 12 pencils cost?
en.e: One pencil costs ₱12; 12 × 12 = 144.

en.q: Solve for x: 2x + 7 = 25.
Twelve coins of ₱5 and ₱10 total ₱85. How many ₱5 coins are there?
A meeting starts at 2:45 p.m. and lasts 3 hours and 30 minutes. When does it end?
The sum of three consecutive integers is 87. What is the largest?
en.e: n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 87 → n = 28, so the largest is 30.

en.q: What is 0.4 × 0.25?
All managers are employees. Some employees work part-time. Which conclusion is certain?
o: None of these conclusions can be drawn with certainty.
en.e: The part-time employees may or may not include managers.

en.q: "If it rains, the event will be cancelled." The event was not cancelled. What follows?
en.e: If the result did not happen, the condition did not happen (modus tollens).

en.q: Which word does not belong: apple, banana, carrot, mango?
en.e: Carrot is a vegetable; the others are fruits.

en.q: If CAT is coded as DBU, how is DOG coded?
en.e: Each letter moves one step forward: D→E, O→P, G→H.

en.q: Ben walks 5 km north, 3 km east, then 5 km south. How far is he from his starting point?
en.e: The north and south walks cancel out, leaving 3 km east.

en.q: A is taller than B. B is taller than C. D is taller than A. Who is the tallest?
en.e: D > A > B > C.

en.q: What comes next: A, C, F, J, O, ___?
en.e: The gaps increase: +2, +3, +4, +5, +6 (O + 6 = U).

en.q: If today is Wednesday, what day is it 100 days from now?
en.e: 100 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 2; two days after Wednesday is Friday.

en.q: No fish are mammals. All whales are mammals. Therefore:
en.e: Whales belong to mammals, and no mammals are fish.

en.q: Pointing to Ana, Ben says, "Her mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is Ben related to Ana?
en.e: The only daughter of Ben's mother is Ben's sister, who is Ana's mother. So Ben is Ana's uncle.

en.q: What comes next: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ___?
en.e: Each number is the sum of the two before it.

en.q: 4 is to 16 as 7 is to:
en.e: The relationship is squaring: 4² = 16, 7² = 49.

en.q: In a survey of 50 people, 30 like coffee, 25 like tea and 10 like both. How many like neither?
What is the angle between the hands of a clock at exactly 3:00?
en.e: Each hour mark is 30°, and 3 × 30° = 90°.

en.q: Which year is a leap year?
en.e: Century years must be divisible by 400 to be leap years.

en.q: What is the missing number: 5, 11, 23, 47, ___?
en.e: Each term is doubled plus 1.

en.q: "Only employees with an ID may enter the building." Jose entered the building, and the rule was followed. What follows?
en.e: If only ID holders may enter and the rule was followed, Jose has an ID.

en.q: Which number does not belong: 121, 144, 169, 175?
en.e: The others are perfect squares (11², 12², 13²).

en.q: Statement: "Use public transport to reduce traffic congestion." Which assumption is implied?
o: More people using public transport means fewer private vehicles on the road.
Traffic is caused only by buses.
en.e: The advice assumes public transport reduces the number of vehicles.

en.q: Five friends sit in a row. Carlo is to the left of Dina. Dina is to the left of Ella. Ana is at the far left. Ben is at the far right. Who sits in the middle?
en.e: Order: Ana, Carlo, Dina, Ella, Ben.

en.q: Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, sovereignty resides in:
en.e: Article II, Section 1: sovereignty resides in the people, and all government authority emanates from them.

en.q: The three branches of the Philippine government are:
en.e: Separation of powers divides authority among these branches.

en.q: The term of office of the President of the Philippines is:
en.e: The President is not eligible for any re-election.

en.q: How many senators are there in the Philippine Senate?
en.e: Senators serve 6-year terms and may not serve more than two consecutive terms.

en.q: Members of the House of Representatives serve terms of:
o: 3 years, up to three consecutive terms
en.e: Voluntary renunciation of office does not interrupt the term count.

en.q: Republic Act No. 6713 is also known as the:
o: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
en.e: RA 6713 sets the norms of conduct for public officials and employees.

en.q: Which is NOT among the norms of conduct under RA 6713?
en.e: The norms include commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, and simple living.

en.q: SALN stands for:
o: Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth
Summary of Annual Leave and Notices
Schedule of Allowances, Leaves and Nominations
Statement of Accounts, Loans and Notes
en.e: Public officials and employees file it under oath, generally every year.

en.q: The central personnel agency of the Philippine government is the:
en.e: The CSC is one of the three independent constitutional commissions.

en.q: The three independent constitutional commissions are:
en.e: Article IX of the Constitution creates these commissions.

en.q: Which office investigates and prosecutes erring public officials?
en.e: The Ombudsman acts on complaints against public officials and employees.

en.q: Under the Ease of Doing Business Act (RA 11032), simple transactions must be completed within:
en.e: Complex transactions: 7 working days; highly technical: 20 working days.

en.q: The Bill of Rights is found in which article of the 1987 Constitution?
en.e: Article III protects rights such as due process and free speech.

en.q: The writ of habeas corpus protects a person against:
en.e: It requires authorities to show the legal basis for holding a person.

en.q: The national language of the Philippines is:
en.e: Filipino and English are the official languages for communication and instruction.

en.q: Republic Act No. 9003 is the:
en.e: It promotes waste segregation, reduction and recycling.

en.q: The Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999 is:
en.e: RA 9275 is the Clean Water Act of 2004.

en.q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations in:
en.e: It sets out fundamental human rights to be universally protected.

en.q: The Commission on Human Rights in the Philippines is:
o: An independent office created by the Constitution
en.e: It investigates human rights violations.

en.q: Under RA 6713, public officials and employees should:
o: Accept gifts from people with pending transactions
Refrain from soliciting or accepting gifts in the course of their official duties
Use office supplies for personal business
en.e: Gifts connected with official duties are generally prohibited, with limited exceptions.

en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to PRUDENT.
en.e: A prudent person thinks carefully before acting and avoids unnecessary risks.

en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to ALLEVIATE.
en.e: To alleviate pain or a problem is to make it less severe.

en.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to SCARCE.
en.e: Scarce means in short supply; abundant means plentiful.

en.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to DILIGENT.
en.e: Diligent means hardworking and attentive; lazy is its opposite.

en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to TACITURN.
en.e: A taciturn person says very little.

en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to EPHEMERAL.
en.e: Something ephemeral lasts only a very short time.

en.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to AMBIGUOUS.
en.e: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation; a clear statement has only one meaning.

en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to CORROBORATE.
en.e: To corroborate a statement is to support or confirm it with evidence.

en.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to MANDATORY.
en.e: A mandatory requirement must be complied with.

en.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to TRANSPARENT.
en.e: Transparent means easy to see through; opaque means not letting light through.

en.q: The committee ___ already submitted its report to the director.
en.e: The committee acts as one unit here (note "its report"), so it takes the singular verb "has."

en.q: If I ___ you, I would accept the transfer to the regional office.
en.e: Hypothetical "if" clauses use the subjunctive "were" for all subjects.

en.q: She has been working in the agency ___ 2019.
en.e: Use "since" with a starting point in time and "for" with a length of time (for five years).

en.q: The certificate of recognition was given to Liza and ___.
en.e: "To" is a preposition, so it takes the object pronoun "me." Test it by removing "Liza and": "given to me."

en.q: One of the computers in the records section ___ not working.
en.e: The subject is "one," which is singular; "of the computers" does not change the verb.

en.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: "The list of requirements / are posted / on the bulletin board / near the entrance."
en.e: The subject is "list" (singular), so the verb should be "is posted."

en.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: "He has went / to the regional office / twice / this month."
en.e: The present perfect uses the past participle: "He has gone."

en.q: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: "The number / of applicants / have increased / this year."
en.e: "The number of" is singular and takes "has increased." (Compare: "A number of applicants have arrived.")

en.q: AUTHOR is to NOVEL as COMPOSER is to:
en.e: The relationship is creator to creation: an author writes a novel; a composer writes a symphony.

en.q: HOT is to COLD as ASCEND is to:
en.e: The pairs are opposites: ascend means go up; descend means go down.

en.q: FINGER is to HAND as TOE is to:
en.e: The relationship is part to whole: a finger is part of a hand; a toe is part of a foot.

en.q: DROUGHT is to WATER as FAMINE is to:
en.e: A drought is a severe shortage of water; a famine is a severe shortage of food.

en.q: THERMOMETER is to TEMPERATURE as BAROMETER is to:
en.e: The relationship is instrument to what it measures. A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

en.q: What does the idiom "once in a blue moon" mean?
en.e: Example: He visits his hometown only once in a blue moon.

en.q: What does the idiom "hit the nail on the head" mean?
en.e: Example: Her analysis hit the nail on the head; that was the real cause of the delay.

en.q: What does the idiom "the ball is in your court" mean?
o: It is your turn to act or decide
The decision has already been made
en.e: Example: We sent our offer, so the ball is in their court now.

en.q: Which spelling is correct?
en.e: Necessary has one "c" and a double "s."

en.q: Choose the correctly spelled word.
en.e: Bureaucracy comes from "bureau" (b-u-r-e-a-u) plus "-cracy."

en.q: The new office rules will take effect ___ January 1.
en.e: Use "on" with specific dates and days (on January 1, on Monday); "in" is for months and years.

en.q: ___ going to submit the documents tomorrow morning.
en.e: "They're" is the contraction of "they are." "Their" shows possession; "there" refers to a place.

en.q: "The barangay health center offers free blood pressure checks every Tuesday and Thursday morning. Residents aged 60 and above may also request home visits." Who may request home visits?
o: Anyone who visits on a Tuesday
en.e: The second sentence limits home visits to residents aged 60 and above.

en.q: "Coral reefs occupy only a tiny fraction of the ocean floor, yet they are home to a large share of all marine species." What point does the sentence emphasize?
o: Coral reefs cover most of the ocean floor
Few species live on coral reefs
Reefs support a lot of marine life for their small size
en.e: "Yet" contrasts the reefs' small area with the large number of species they support.

en.q: "The agency replaced its paper-based filing system with a digital one. As a result, documents that once took days to locate can now be retrieved in minutes." What was the effect of the change?
o: Documents are now harder to find
The agency hired more file clerks
Documents can be found much faster
en.e: "As a result" introduces the effect: retrieval time dropped from days to minutes.

en.q: "Contrary to popular belief, bats are not blind. Most species can see, and many also use echolocation to find their way in the dark." Which statement is supported by the passage?
o: Bats can see, and many also use echolocation
Bats cannot move about in the dark
en.e: The passage says most bats can see and many also use echolocation.

en.q: "Mr. Reyes reviewed the proposal and found several errors in the budget. He returned it to the team with a note asking them to revise the figures before Friday." What did Mr. Reyes ask the team to do?
o: Revise the budget figures before Friday
Submit a new proposal on Friday
en.e: His note asked the team to revise the figures before Friday.

en.q: "The new director was known for her terse e-mails; most of them were no longer than a single line." The word "terse" most nearly means:
en.e: The clue is that most of her e-mails were only one line long.

en.q: "Regular exercise strengthens the heart, improves mood and helps control weight. Even a brisk 30-minute walk on most days can make a difference." What is the main idea?
o: Even moderate regular exercise has several health benefits
Walking is better than all other exercise
Exercise is mainly for losing weight
en.e: The passage lists several benefits and notes that even a brisk walk helps.

en.q: "The library extended its hours during the examination period so that students would have more time to study." Why did the library extend its hours?
o: To give students more time to study
To reduce the number of visitors
en.e: The phrase "so that" introduces the purpose.

en.q: "When Liza arrived at the office, the lights were off, the door was locked, and the guard told her that everyone had left an hour earlier." What can be inferred?
o: Liza was the first to arrive in the morning
The office had moved to a new building
Liza arrived after her co-workers had gone home
The guard had lost the key
en.e: Everyone had already left, so she came after the others had gone.

en.q: "We are deeply grateful to the volunteers who gave up their weekends to rebuild the school after the flood." The tone of the statement is:
en.e: "Deeply grateful" expresses appreciation.

en.q: "Some people think that saving money requires a high income. In fact, small amounts set aside regularly can grow into substantial savings over time." What does the author suggest?
o: Only the rich can save money
People should spend all their income
People do not need a high income to build savings
en.e: "In fact" introduces the author's view, which corrects the common belief.

en.q: "Starting Monday, the bridge will be closed to heavy trucks. Private cars and motorcycles may still cross, but only one lane will be open." Which vehicles may NOT use the bridge starting Monday?
en.e: Only heavy trucks are barred; cars and motorcycles may still cross on one lane.

en.q: Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph: (1) Then, the water is filtered to remove particles. (2) Finally, it is disinfected and stored in tanks. (3) First, water is drawn from the river.
en.e: The signal words First, Then and Finally give the order.

en.q: "(1) Manila is the capital of the Philippines. (2) It lies on the eastern shore of Manila Bay. (3) It is home to Intramuros, the old walled city. (4) It is the most interesting city in Asia." Which sentence expresses an opinion?
en.e: "Most interesting" is a personal judgment that cannot be proven; sentences 1 to 3 can be checked as facts.

en.q: "A farmer noticed that the plants near the canal grew taller than those on the hill. He concluded that the extra water made the difference." What did the farmer think caused the difference in height?
o: The plants near the canal got more water
The plants on the hill got more sunlight
The canal plants were planted earlier
en.e: He concluded that the extra water near the canal made the plants taller.

en.q: "The mayor's proposal was met with skepticism; many residents doubted that the project could be finished on time." The word "skepticism" most nearly means:
en.e: The clue is that residents "doubted" the project could be finished on time.

en.q: "Unlike the old policy, which required three signatures, the new policy requires only the approval of the division chief." How does the new policy differ from the old one?
o: It requires no approval at all
en.e: The old policy needed three signatures; the new one needs only one approval.

en.q: "Social media allows government agencies to share announcements quickly. However, agencies must also guard against the spread of false information on these platforms." Which is the best title?
o: Social Media in Government: Benefits and Risks
How to Open a Social Media Account
Why Agencies Should Stop Using Social Media
en.e: The passage gives one benefit (speed) and one risk (false information).

en.q: "The seminar is open to all employees. Those who wish to attend must register online by March 10. Seats are limited to 50 participants." Which detail is NOT stated in the notice?
en.e: The notice says nothing about certificates.

en.q: "Ramon had saved for months to buy a laptop. When the store announced a sale, he rushed there, only to find that the model he wanted was sold out." How did Ramon most likely feel?
en.e: He had worked toward the purchase, and the model he wanted was gone.

en.q: "Because the road was being repaired, the jeepneys took a longer route, and many passengers arrived late for work." Why did many passengers arrive late?
o: The jeepney drivers were on strike
Road repairs forced the jeepneys to take a longer route
There were fewer jeepneys that day
en.e: The road repair (cause) led to a longer route, which made passengers late (effect).

en.q: A sign at the beach reads: "No swimming beyond the red buoys. No lifeguard on duty after 5 p.m." What can be inferred?
o: Swimming is not allowed at the beach
People swimming after 5 p.m. will not be watched by a lifeguard
The lifeguard works only at night
The red buoys mark the shallowest area
en.e: The second line means no lifeguard is present after 5 p.m.

en.q: "To apply for the scholarship, complete the form, attach your latest grades, and submit both to the registrar by June 15." What is the main purpose of the text?
en.e: It lists the steps an applicant must follow.

en.q: "Although the town is small, it hosts a festival every year that attracts thousands of visitors from across the country." What does the sentence suggest?
o: The town is one of the largest in the country
The festival is popular despite the town's small size
The festival is held every month
en.e: "Although" sets the town's small size against the festival's large crowds.

en.q: "The evidence was so compelling that the investigating panel reached a decision in less than an hour." The word "compelling" most nearly means:
en.e: Strong, convincing evidence allowed a quick decision.

en.q: "Recycling saves resources. For example, recycling paper reduces the number of trees that must be cut down." What is the role of the second sentence?
o: It gives an example that supports the first sentence
en.e: "For example" signals a supporting example.

en.q: "The clinic will be closed on Saturday for repairs. Patients with appointments on that day will be called to reschedule." What will happen to Saturday's appointments?
o: They will push through as planned
They will be cancelled with no new date
They will be held at another clinic
They will be moved to another date
en.e: The patients will be called to reschedule, meaning a new date will be set.

en.q: "Many Filipino families have members working abroad who send money home. These remittances help pay for education, housing and daily needs." What is the main idea?
o: Education in the Philippines is free
Families should not depend on relatives
Money sent home from abroad supports families in many ways
en.e: The passage explains how remittances help families.

en.q: "It is unacceptable that, after three years, the streetlights on this road have still not been repaired." The tone of the statement is:
en.e: "Unacceptable" and "still not been repaired" show strong disapproval.

en.q: "Despite the heavy traffic, Rosa arrived at the interview ten minutes early because she had left her house two hours ahead of time." What can be inferred about Rosa?
o: She lives next to the venue
en.e: Leaving two hours early to beat traffic shows planning.

en.q: What is 12% of 850?
A ₱500 item is marked up by 20%, then the new price is reduced by 20%. What is the final price?
en.e: After the increase: 500 × 1.20 = 600. After the decrease: 600 × 0.80 = 480. The two 20% changes do not cancel because they apply to different bases.

en.q: 18 is what percent of 72?
After a 10% salary increase, Ben now earns ₱27,500 a month. What was his salary before the increase?
en.e: New salary = 110% of old salary. 27,500 ÷ 1.10 = 25,000. (Subtracting 10% of 27,500 gives 24,750, which is wrong because the 10% was based on the old salary.)

en.q: The ratio of boys to girls in a class of 36 is 4:5. How many girls are there?
en.e: 4 + 5 = 9 parts; 36 ÷ 9 = 4 per part; girls = 5 × 4 = 20.

en.q: Pipe A can fill a tank in 4 hours. Pipe B can empty the full tank in 6 hours. If both pipes are open, how long will it take to fill the empty tank?
en.e: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/6 = 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12 tank per hour, so it takes 12 hours.

en.q: Six workers can finish a project in 10 days. At the same rate, how many days will 15 workers need?
en.e: Total work = 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days; 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.

en.q: A car travels at 60 km/h for 2 hours and then at 90 km/h for 1 hour. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
en.e: Distance = 60 × 2 + 90 × 1 = 210 km; time = 3 hours. Average speed = 210 ÷ 3 = 70 km/h (not the simple average of the two speeds, 75).

en.q: Two towns are 180 km apart. Two cars leave the towns at the same time and drive toward each other at 50 km/h and 40 km/h. After how many hours will they meet?
en.e: They close the gap at 50 + 40 = 90 km/h; 180 ÷ 90 = 2 hours.

en.q: What comes next in the series 4, 7, 12, 19, 28, ___?
en.e: The differences are 3, 5, 7, 9 (odd numbers), so the next difference is 11: 28 + 11 = 39.

en.q: What comes next in the series 100, 95, 85, 70, 50, ___?
en.e: The amounts subtracted are 5, 10, 15, 20, so the next is 25: 50 − 25 = 25.

en.q: What comes next in the series 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ___?
en.e: Multiply by 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6: 120 × 6 = 720.

en.q: What comes next in the series 2, 10, 4, 20, 8, 40, ___?
en.e: Two series alternate: 2, 4, 8, ... and 10, 20, 40, ..., each doubling. The next term continues the first series: 8 × 2 = 16.

en.q: What is 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4?
en.e: 2 1/2 = 5/2. Dividing by 1/4 means multiplying by 4: 5/2 × 4 = 10.

en.q: What is 3.6 ÷ 0.12?
en.e: Multiply both numbers by 100: 360 ÷ 12 = 30.

en.q: ₱8,000 earns ₱960 in simple interest after 2 years. What is the annual interest rate?
₱10,000 is deposited at 10% interest compounded annually. How much is in the account after 2 years?
en.e: Year 1: 10,000 × 1.10 = 11,000. Year 2: 11,000 × 1.10 = 12,100. (Simple interest would give only 12,000.)

en.q: In 5 years, Ana will be twice as old as she was 5 years ago. How old is Ana now?
en.e: Let x be her age now: x + 5 = 2(x − 5) → x + 5 = 2x − 10 → x = 15.

en.q: Pedro is 8 years older than Juan. Four years ago, Pedro was twice as old as Juan. How old is Juan now?
en.e: Let J be Juan's age now; Pedro is J + 8. Four years ago: (J + 8) − 4 = 2(J − 4) → J + 4 = 2J − 8 → J = 12. (Pedro is 20.)

en.q: The average of five numbers is 18. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four is 16. What number was removed?
en.e: Sum of five = 5 × 18 = 90; sum of four = 4 × 16 = 64; removed number = 90 − 64 = 26.

en.q: A class has 40 students, and 35% of them are boys. How many girls are in the class?
A vendor buys an item for ₱800 and sells it for ₱1,000. What is the percent profit based on cost?
en.e: Profit = 1,000 − 800 = 200; 200 ÷ 800 = 0.25 = 25%. (Dividing by the selling price gives 20%, which is not based on cost.)

en.q: A ₱2,000 appliance is discounted 20%, and an additional 10% is taken off the discounted price. What is the final price?
en.e: After 20% off: 2,000 × 0.80 = 1,600. After another 10% off: 1,600 × 0.90 = 1,440. (A flat 30% off would give 1,400.)

en.q: On a map, 1 cm represents 5 km. Two towns are 7.5 cm apart on the map. What is the actual distance?
Three bells ring every 6, 8 and 12 minutes. If they ring together at 8:00 a.m., when will they next ring together?
en.e: They ring together after the least common multiple of 6, 8 and 12, which is 24 minutes: 8:24 a.m.

en.q: Solve for x: 5x − 3 = 2x + 15.
A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area?
en.e: Side = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm; area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

en.q: What is the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 14 cm? (Use π = 22/7.)
en.e: C = πd = 22/7 × 14 = 44 cm. (154 cm² is the area, not the circumference.)

en.q: An employee earns ₱650 a day and works 22 days in a month. Monthly deductions total ₱1,800. What is the net monthly pay?
A printer prints 24 pages per minute. How long will it take to print 1,080 pages?
All teachers in the school are college graduates. Maria is a teacher in the school. Which conclusion follows?
o: Maria is not a college graduate.
Some teachers are not college graduates.
en.e: Maria belongs to the group of teachers, and every member of that group is a graduate.

en.q: Some clerks are typists. All typists are trained in records management. Which conclusion must be true?
o: All clerks are trained in records management.
Some clerks are trained in records management.
No clerk is trained in records management.
en.e: The clerks who are typists are trained, so at least some clerks are trained. Nothing is known about the other clerks.

en.q: Which statement is logically equivalent to "If a document is signed, it is valid"?
o: If a document is not valid, it is not signed.
If a document is valid, it is signed.
If a document is not signed, it is not valid.
A document is signed only if it is not valid.
en.e: The contrapositive (if not Q, then not P) is always equivalent. The converse and inverse are not.

en.q: What comes next: B, E, H, K, ___?
en.e: Each letter moves 3 places forward: B → E → H → K → N.

en.q: What comes next: Z, X, U, Q, ___?
en.e: The letters move back 2, 3, 4, then 5 places: Q − 5 = L.

en.q: What comes next: AZ, BY, CX, ___?
en.e: The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) and the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W).

en.q: If MANILA is written as ALINAM, how is CEBU written in the same code?
en.e: The code writes the word backward: CEBU → UBEC.

en.q: If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 and so on, the word BAD has a value of 2 + 1 + 4 = 7. What is the value of FACE?
Which number does not belong: 3, 5, 9, 11?
en.e: 3, 5 and 11 are prime numbers; 9 = 3 × 3 is not prime. All four are odd, so oddness is not the rule.

en.q: Which word does not belong: triangle, square, pentagon, cube?
en.e: A cube is a three-dimensional solid; the others are flat (two-dimensional) shapes.

en.q: What is the next number: 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 17, ___?
en.e: The differences increase by 1: +1, +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next is +6: 17 + 6 = 23.

en.q: What is the next number: 81, 27, 9, 3, ___?
en.e: Each term is divided by 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

en.q: Of 40 employees, 25 speak Cebuano, 20 speak Ilocano and 8 speak neither language. How many speak both?
en.e: Employees who speak at least one = 40 − 8 = 32. Both = 25 + 20 − 32 = 13.

en.q: Leo faces north. He turns 90° to his right, then another 90° to his right, then 90° to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
en.e: North → right → East → right → South → left → East.

en.q: Mila walks 6 km east and then 8 km north. What is the straight-line distance from her starting point?
en.e: The path forms a right triangle: √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 km.

en.q: Lito, who has no brothers, points to a man and says, "That man's father is my father's only son." How is the man related to Lito?
en.e: Lito has no brothers, so his father's only son is Lito himself. The man's father is Lito, so the man is Lito's son.

en.q: Rosa is Carlo's sister. Carlo is Dan's father. How is Rosa related to Dan?
en.e: Rosa is the sister of Dan's father, so she is Dan's aunt.

en.q: In a row of students, Mark is 7th from the left and 12th from the right. How many students are in the row?
en.e: 7 + 12 − 1 = 18. Subtract 1 because Mark is counted in both positions.

en.q: If March 1 falls on a Monday, what day of the week is March 25 of the same year?
en.e: March 25 is 24 days after March 1. 24 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 3, and three days after Monday is Thursday.

en.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 4:30?
What is the value of x? (1) x + y = 10 (2) x − y = 4
o: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but (2) alone is not.
Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but (1) alone is not.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is.
The statements together are still not sufficient.
en.e: Each equation alone has two unknowns. Together: adding them gives 2x = 14, so x = 7.

en.q: Is the integer n even? (1) n is divisible by 4. (2) n is greater than 10.
o: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but (2) alone is not.
Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but (1) alone is not.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is.
The statements together are still not sufficient.
en.e: Any multiple of 4 is even, so (1) answers the question. (2) does not: 11 and 12 are both greater than 10.

en.q: What is the price of one pen? (1) Three pens and two pencils cost ₱54 in all. (2) A pencil costs less than a pen.
o: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but (2) alone is not.
Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but (1) alone is not.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is.
The statements together are still not sufficient.
en.e: Many prices fit both facts (e.g. pen ₱14 and pencil ₱6, or pen ₱16 and pencil ₱3), so the price of a pen cannot be found.

en.q: Statement: "The agency posted its job openings on its website to attract more applicants." Which assumption is implied?
o: The agency has too many employees.
Potential applicants visit the agency's website.
Only website visitors are qualified for the jobs.
en.e: Posting online would attract applicants only if job seekers actually look at the website.

en.q: All 12 employees in Unit A passed the exam. Rina passed the exam. Which statement is correct?
o: Whether Rina is in Unit A cannot be determined.
Rina is not in Unit A.
Everyone who passed is in Unit A.
en.e: The statement says all of Unit A passed, not that only Unit A passed. Rina may be from another unit.

en.q: A, B, C and D sit around a square table, one on each side, facing the center. A sits opposite C, and B sits on A's right. Who sits on A's left?
en.e: C takes the seat opposite A, and B takes A's right, so the only seat left, on A's left, belongs to D.

en.q: Five boxes have different weights. P is heavier than Q but lighter than R. S is lighter than Q. T is heavier than R. Which box is the third heaviest?
en.e: From heaviest to lightest: T, R, P, Q, S. The third heaviest is P.

en.q: 2 is to 8 as 3 is to 27. Following the same rule, 4 is to:
en.e: Each number is cubed: 2³ = 8, 3³ = 27, 4³ = 64.

en.q: Which number does not belong: 27, 36, 45, 52?
en.e: 27, 36 and 45 are multiples of 9; 52 is not.

en.q: Find the missing number: 3 → 10, 4 → 17, 5 → 26, 6 → ___
en.e: Each number is squared and then 1 is added: 6² + 1 = 37.

en.q: Article I of the 1987 Philippine Constitution deals with:
en.e: Article I defines the national territory; Article III is the Bill of Rights, Article IV citizenship and Article V suffrage.

en.q: Under the 1987 Constitution, the Philippines renounces war as:
en.e: Article II, Section 2: the Philippines renounces war as an instrument of national policy.

en.q: According to the Declaration of Principles in the 1987 Constitution, which authority is supreme at all times?
o: Local authority, over the national government
en.e: Article II, Section 3: civilian authority is, at all times, supreme over the military.

en.q: Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Constitution directs the State to protect and advance the people's right to:
en.e: The right to a balanced and healthful ecology is to be protected in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.

en.q: What is the minimum age, on the day of the election, to be elected President of the Philippines?
en.e: The President must be a natural-born citizen, a registered voter, able to read and write, at least 40 years old and a resident for at least 10 years before the election.

en.q: What is the minimum age, on the day of the election, to be elected Senator?
en.e: A Senator must be at least 35 years old and a resident of the Philippines for at least two years before the election.

en.q: Under the 1987 Constitution, the Vice President:
o: Serves a 6-year term and is not eligible for any re-election
Serves a 3-year term and may serve up to three consecutive terms
Serves a 4-year term and may be re-elected for one more term
Serves a 6-year term and may not serve more than two successive terms
en.e: Article VII, Section 4: the Vice President has a 6-year term and may not serve more than two successive terms.

en.q: The Supreme Court of the Philippines is composed of:
o: A Chief Justice and 12 Associate Justices
A Chief Justice and 8 Associate Justices
A Chief Justice and 14 Associate Justices
15 Associate Justices with a rotating head
en.e: Article VIII, Section 4: the Court has a Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices, for a total of 15 members.

en.q: Under the 1987 Constitution, a proclamation of martial law by the President may initially last for a period not exceeding:
en.e: Article VII, Section 18. Congress may revoke the proclamation or, on the President's initiative, extend it.

en.q: Which body has the sole power to declare the existence of a state of war?
en.e: Article VI, Section 23(1): Congress, by a vote of two-thirds of both Houses in joint session assembled, voting separately, has the sole power to declare the existence of a state of war.

en.q: In impeachment proceedings, which body has the sole power to try and decide the case?
en.e: The House has the exclusive power to initiate impeachment cases; the Senate tries and decides them (Article XI, Section 3).

en.q: Under the 1987 Constitution, who may grant reprieves, commutations and pardons after conviction by final judgment, except in cases of impeachment?
en.e: Article VII, Section 19 gives this power to the President.

en.q: The Civil Service Commission is composed of:
o: A Chairman and six regional directors
en.e: Article IX-B, Section 1: they serve a term of seven years without reappointment.

en.q: Under the 1987 Constitution, appointments in the civil service shall be made only according to:
en.e: Merit and fitness is determined, as far as practicable, by competitive examination, except for policy-determining, primarily confidential or highly technical positions.

en.q: Which activity does the 1987 Constitution prohibit for officers and employees in the civil service?
o: Engaging in electioneering or partisan political campaigns
en.e: Article IX-B, Section 2(4). The same section protects government employees' right to self-organization.

en.q: Article XI of the 1987 Constitution, on the accountability of public officers, opens with which principle?
o: Public office is a public trust.
Civilian authority is supreme over the military.
The State values the dignity of every human person.
en.e: Public officers must at all times be accountable to the people and serve them with responsibility, integrity, loyalty and efficiency.

en.q: Under Article V of the 1987 Constitution, what is the minimum age to vote?
en.e: Voters must also have lived in the Philippines for at least one year, and in the place where they will vote for at least six months, before the election.

en.q: The 1987 Constitution directs the State to assign the highest budgetary priority to:
en.e: Article XIV, Section 5(5).

en.q: The 1987 Constitution was ratified in a nationwide plebiscite held on:
en.e: February 25, 1986 marks the end of the EDSA People Power Revolution; the new Constitution was ratified the following year.

en.q: Philippine independence from Spain was proclaimed on June 12, 1898 in:
en.e: General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed independence at his house in Kawit. Malolos later became the seat of the First Republic.

en.q: Under RA 6713, the norm that requires public officials and employees to lead modest lives and avoid any extravagant display of wealth is:
en.e: Simple living: they shall lead modest lives appropriate to their positions and income.

en.q: Under RA 6713, providing service to everyone without unfair discrimination and regardless of party affiliation or preference describes:
en.e: This is the definition of political neutrality in Section 4 of RA 6713.

en.q: Under RA 6713, the norm of commitment to public interest requires public officials and employees to:
o: Give priority to their superiors' personal requests
Promote the interests of their political party
Uphold the public interest over and above personal interest
en.e: Section 4(A)(a) of RA 6713.

en.q: Under RA 6713, within how many working days from receipt must public officials and employees respond to letters and requests from the public?
en.e: Section 5(a): the reply must state the action taken on the request.

en.q: Under RA 6713, public officials and employees must file their SALN annually on or before:
en.e: It is also filed within 30 days after assuming office and within 30 days after leaving the service.

en.q: Under RA 6713, when a conflict of interest arises, a public official must divest his or her shareholdings or interest in the business within how many days from assuming office?
en.e: Section 9: resign from any position in the private enterprise within 30 days, and divest shareholdings or interest within 60 days.

en.q: The writ of kalikasan is a legal remedy against:
o: Illegal arrest or detention of a person by government authorities
Environmental damage that threatens life, health or property in two or more cities or provinces
Refusal of a government office to release public records
Unauthorized gathering or use of a person's private data
en.e: It is provided in the Supreme Court's Rules of Procedure for Environmental Cases. Unlawful detention is addressed by habeas corpus, and misuse of private data by habeas data.

en.q: The writ of amparo is a remedy available to any person whose right to ___ is violated or threatened by an unlawful act or omission of a public official or employee, or of a private individual or entity.
en.e: It is commonly used in cases of extralegal killings and enforced disappearances, or threats of them.

en.q: The Geneva Conventions are core treaties of international humanitarian law, which aims mainly to:
o: Promote free trade among member states
Settle boundary disputes between neighboring countries
Limit the effects of armed conflict and protect those not taking part in hostilities
Protect the rights of workers employed abroad
en.e: International humanitarian law protects civilians, the wounded and sick, and prisoners of war.

en.q: The Climate Change Act of 2009, which created the Climate Change Commission, is:
en.e: RA 8749 is the Clean Air Act, RA 9275 the Clean Water Act and RA 9003 the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act.
